Consumer and Business Sentiment 
After improving strongly through most of the first quarter in 2020, measures of consumer and 
business sentiment pulled back in March 2020 as social distancing and business closures took 
effect.  The Reuters/Michigan consumer sentiment index rose to 101.0 in February 2020, just shy 
of the 14-year high reached in 2018, the subsequently fell by more than 29 points.  This index 
trended higher for several months, reaching 88.3 in April 2021.  Since then, however, this index 
has trended lower, and dropped sharply in early August to 70.2, or 1.6 points below the pandemic 
low reached in April 2020.  The 11-point drop in early August, one of the sharpest in the 
survey’s history, reflected renewed concerns among consumers about the impact of the delta 
variant on the economy.  From a pre-pandemic level of 132.6 in February 2020, the Conference
